title: A practice plan
goal: Outlines are half; speed comes from short daily practice on the words you miss.

items: **Lessons 2 to 7 first.** Drill until they pass cleanly twice. Accuracy before speed.
**Lesson 8 in slices.** Ten common words a session, then mixed practice; they are most of what you type.
**Lessons 10 to 13 by use.** Learn an ending when you need it; do not memorise the whole table.
**Lessons 14 to 16 last.** Phrases, punctuation and letters, once words are fluent.
**Ten to twenty minutes**, once a day, beats an hour once a week.
Start with what you passed yesterday (Practice, mixed).
Then new material: one drill, or ten words.
End with **your misses**: a Practice button drills the words you keep getting wrong.

blocks.x: When you are stuck on a word

items: **Lookup** shows the fastest outline and the other ways in.
No one-stroke form? Say it, split it, join the syllables (lesson 12).
Always hold the join key on every stroke after the first.

blocks.x: These drills read an ordinary keyboard. Once the outlines are learned, move to a steno keyboard or keyboard mapper with the generated dictionary (`lyk build`, `lyk deploy`: [Build and files](#/ref/build-and-files)) and practise on text you want to write.
`lyk mistakes --drill` turns the misstrokes on your steno tape into a personal drill set for this site (Practice, My drills).
Every rule, table and mechanism these lessons teach is in the [Reference](#/ref), starting at the [cheat sheet](#/ref/cheatsheet). Maintainer logs: `docs/decisions.md` in the repository.
